rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a sudden strong impulse to do something.

example.english: I suddenly had an urge to quit immediately.
example.traditional: 我突然有衝動，想即刻辭職。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dat6 jin4 jau5 cung1 dung6 soeng2 zik1 hak1 ci4 zik1

rows.note: Use this for a deep longing or strong desire, especially for an object, experience, or outcome rather than a sudden impulse.

example.english: They have long had an urge to visit the Arctic to see the northern lights.
example.traditional: 佢一直渴望有機會去北極睇極光。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jat1 zik6 hot3 mong6 jau5 gei1 wui6 heoi3 bak1 gik6 tai2 gik6 gwong1

rows.note: Use this for a strong desire treated as a lasting want, often with physical, emotional, or sexual overtones.

example.english: Suppressing an urge for a long time can be very painful.
example.traditional: 長期壓抑慾望，個人會好辛苦。
example.jyutping: coeng4 kei4 aat3 jik1 juk6 mong6 go3 jan4 wui5 hou2 san1 fu2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for trying to persuade someone to do something.

example.english: I urge him to try this restaurant.
example.jyutping: ngo5 hyun3 keoi5 si3 haa5 ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1

rows.note: Use this when the pressure involves hurrying or repeatedly pushing someone to act.

example.english: You always urge me to hurry up; I’m almost done.
example.traditional: 你成日催我快啲，我就快做完喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 seng4 jat6 ceoi1 ngo5 faai3 di1 ngo5 zau6 faai3 zou6 jyun4 laa3

rows.note: Use this when urging something means insisting on a position, argument, or requirement.

example.english: The committee urge us to retain this requirement.
example.traditional: 委員會堅持要我哋保留呢項規定。
example.jyutping: wai2 jyun4 wui6 gin1 ci4 jiu3 ngo5 dei6 bou2 lau4 ni1 hong6 kwai1 ding6

rows.note: Use this formal verb when strongly advocating a particular argument, policy, or course of action.

example.english: We urge the government to strengthen regulation immediately.
example.traditional: 本會力主政府立即加強監管。
example.jyutping: bun2 wui5 lik6 zyu2 zing3 fu2 lap6 zik1 gaa1 koeng4 gaam1 gun2
